headline: Non-smartphone users pay £264 more annually for bus passes due to app-exclusive deals
summary: Many bus companies and supermarkets now offer cheaper deals exclusively through smartphone apps, penalizing those who don't use them or prefer non-standard operating systems.
details: Owen Fraser highlights how bus companies penalize non-smartphone users with higher fares. He notes that he spends an extra £264 annually on bus passes because cheaper monthly options are exclusive to apps he cannot use.
Fraser uses a non-standard operating system to avoid the "always-online" models of Android and iOS. This choice forces him to buy more expensive weekly passes instead of app-exclusive monthly ones.

The issue extends beyond bus travel, with many supermarket loyalty schemes also becoming app-only. This trend creates a barrier to accessible public transport and essential services for a segment of the population.

He argues that access to public transport should not depend on a passenger's choice of computer software, especially amidst the current cost of living crisis. The article calls for a unified approach to address the ill effects of such technology.

headline: AI is making restaurant menus easier to navigate via nutrition insights and smart recommendations.
summary: AI-powered food tech is transforming dining by offering detailed breakdowns of calories, allergens, and personalized recommendations, even from handwritten menus. This democratizes nutrition transparency for all restaurants.
details: AI-powered food tech is making restaurant menus easier to navigate, providing nutrition insights, allergen warnings, and personalized recommendations. This transformation is driven by natural language processing and data science, interpreting and enriching menu information at scale.

Diners can snap a photo of any menu, even handwritten, to receive a detailed breakdown of calories, allergen warnings, and vegan options. This level of transparency is quickly becoming an expectation for digitally savvy customers.

AI menu analysis starts with text recognition and interpretation, deciphering descriptions and predicting nutrition facts using deep learning and vast ingredient databases. This democratizes nutrition transparency for all restaurants, including small independents.

For diners, this means no more guesswork or awkward questions about dietary suitability, while advanced systems can flag allergens and adapt recommendations in real-time. This empowers diners with actionable restaurant nutrition data.

The move towards smart menus allows dynamic, AI-powered systems to adapt to individual preferences, filtering and ranking dishes for each diner. These systems can also surface dishes fitting complex dietary patterns like keto or Mediterranean.

Companies like Bite AI, MenuSifu, and LeanDine are leading this trend, offering solutions that blend nutrition science, machine learning, and seamless user experience. These platforms bring AI intelligence directly to the dining experience.
